observation: Windows passed the batch naming and two FreeCAD CLI compatibility checks, but all eight FreeCAD open/insert cases failed immediately with 'no such file or directory'. The pinned FreeCAD executable existed and each generated DWG passed installed-converter strict preflight.
cause: A direct CMake process-launch reproduction showed list(REMOVE_ITEM) strips the escaped semicolons from the already-added Windows PATH item. Expanding the reconstructed environment list makes cmake -E env interpret a PATH fragment as the executable.
change: Append the escaped PATH argument only after all list removals, immediately before the process launch.
validation: A direct CMake control reproduces the original error and passes after the same argument-order correction, preserving all three semicolon-separated path components through process launch.
limits: This local CMake control is not a Windows FreeCAD execution. The eight native application checks require a fresh Windows run, and no support claim is promoted.
